scenario.title: 朋友分手了，怎麼陪伴和給建議
scenario.context: 朋友失戀時，給建議要非常小心：太直接像在說教，太模糊又沒幫助。英文用 You could… / You might… / Why don't you…? / Maybe try… 讓建議聽起來像選項，而不是命令。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Oh, Amy. I'm so sorry. Come here.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: Three years, and he couldn't even call me.
lines.zh: 三年了，他連打通電話都不肯。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: That's awful. You deserved so much better than that.
lines.zh: 太爛了，你值得更好的對待。

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: I don't even know what to do with myself right now.
lines.zh: 我現在都不知道該怎麼辦。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Why don't you stay at my place this weekend? We could order food and watch terrible movies.
lines.zh: 你這週末要不要住我家？我們可以叫外送看爛片。

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: I think I'm ready to move on. But everyone keeps saying there are plenty of fish in the sea.
lines.zh: 我想我準備好往前走了。但大家一直說天涯何處無芳草。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Ugh, that's the least helpful thing to say.
lines.zh: 唉，那是最沒幫助的一句話。

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: Right? And I don't want a rebound. I just want to feel like myself again.
lines.zh: 對吧？而且我不想找個人填補空虛，我只想重新找回自己。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: You might try doing something just for you. What about that ceramics class you wanted to take?
lines.zh: 你可以試試做些只為自己的事。你之前想上的陶藝課呢？

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: I could sign up. I always put it off because of him.
lines.zh: 我可以報名。我以前一直因為他拖延。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Maybe it's time. And you could come to my Thursday dinner club too, if you feel like it.
lines.zh: 也許是時候了。如果你想的話，也可以來我的週四晚餐聚會。

patterns.en: I'm so sorry. That must be really hard.
patterns.zh: 我很遺憾，那一定很難受。

patterns.en: Do you want to talk about it?
Take all the time you need.

chinglish.wrong: Don't be sad, next one will be better.
chinglish.right: I'm so sorry. You deserve someone who treats you well.
chinglish.why: 「別難過」直翻聽起來像在否定對方的感受。先同理，再鼓勵。

chinglish.right: Take your time. You'll get through this.
chinglish.why: should 太像命令，而且「快點忘了他」對剛失戀的人壓力很大。

chinglish.right: He broke up with you. / He dumped you.
chinglish.why: break up 要加 with + 人。

chinglish.wrong: You can try to go out more.
chinglish.right: You could try going out more.
chinglish.why: can 比較像「你有能力」，給建議用 could 更委婉；try V-ing = 試試某方法（複習第 71 單元）。

grammar.title: could / might / Why don't you 建議
grammar.oneLiner: 給建議從強到弱：You should > Why don't you…? > You could… > You might (want to)… > Maybe you could…
whenToUse: You could + V：提供一個選項。You could take a trip.
You might + V / might want to：更委婉。You might try yoga.
Why don't you + V?：友善的提議。Why don't you stay with me?
Why not + V?：更簡短。Why not take a class?
How about / What about + V-ing / 名詞：How about going for a walk?
If I were you, I'd…（第 45 單元）
注意：Why don't you…? 不是在問原因，而是在提建議，語調要下降。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文的「你可以」「你應該」「要不要」差別不大，都算正常建議。英文卻很講究：should 在情緒敏感的時候聽起來太強勢。另外，台灣人第一次聽到 Why don't you…? 常常以為對方在問「你為什麼不…」，會開始解釋理由，其實對方只是在給建議。

examples.correct: Why don't you take a few days off?
examples.note: 友善的建議，不是在問原因。

examples.correct: You could try journaling. It helped me.
examples.note: 提供選項 + 個人經驗。

examples.correct: You might want to talk to a counselor.
How about going for a walk by the river?
examples.incorrect: How about go for a walk?

examples.correct: Maybe you could call your sister.

quiz.question: Which is the gentlest suggestion?
options: You might try going out a bit more.

quiz.question: Why ___ you come over for dinner?
quiz.explanation: Why don't you…? = 你要不要…？

quiz.question: A friend says, "Why don't you join us?" This means:
options: They want to know your reason.
quiz.explanation: Why don't you…? 是邀請或建議。

quiz.question: You ___ try talking to him directly. (提供選項)

slang.term: plenty of fish in the sea
slang.usage: 安慰失戀的人還有很多對象。

risk.note: 剛失戀就說可能顯得敷衍，時機很重要。

examples.en: Don't worry. There are plenty of fish in the sea.
examples.zh: 別擔心，天涯何處無芳草。

examples.en: Everyone says there are plenty of fish in the sea, but I want this fish!
examples.zh: 大家都說天涯何處無芳草，但我就要這一株！

slang.usage: 從失戀、失敗或困難中走出來。move on from something。

risk.note: 常見用語；催別人 Just move on 會顯得不體貼。

examples.en: It took me a year to move on after the breakup.
examples.zh: 分手後我花了一年才走出來。

examples.en: It's time to move on to the next project.
examples.zh: 是時候進行下一個案子了。

slang.usage: dump someone = 跟某人分手（主動方）。get dumped = 被甩。

examples.en: She dumped him the day before Valentine's.
examples.zh: 她在情人節前一天把他甩了。

examples.en: I got dumped in college, and it was the best thing that happened to me.
examples.zh: 我大學時被甩，那是發生在我身上最好的事。

slang.meaning: 分手後馬上找來填補空虛的對象
slang.usage: a rebound (relationship) / on the rebound = 失戀後的空窗期。

risk.note: 說別人的新對象是 rebound 可能很傷人。

examples.en: Be careful. You don't want a rebound relationship.
examples.zh: 小心點，你不會想要一段填補空虛的感情。

examples.en: I think he's just her rebound.
examples.zh: 我覺得他只是她失戀後的過渡。

review.question: It wasn't the breakup ___ hurt. It was the way he did it.
review.explanation: 複習第 72 單元：It was… that。

review.question: I've stopped ___ his social media. It's healthier.
review.explanation: 複習第 71 單元：stop V-ing = 不再做。

review.question: The ___ you think about him, the worse you'll feel. (越多)
review.explanation: 複習第 69 單元：the more… the worse…

review.question: She deleted his number so ___ she wouldn't text him.
Her ex, ___ she dated for three years, moved to Canada.
review.explanation: 複習第 57 單元：非限定子句不用 that。

review.question: I'll pick ___ at your place at 7.
review.explanation: 複習第 41 單元：代名詞放中間。

review.question: He was supposed to come, but he ___ at the last minute.
review.explanation: 複習第 9 單元：bail 過去式。

review.question: Which is the gentlest suggestion?
options: You could try a new hobby.
review.explanation: You could… 提供選項最溫和。
